text: Article 114. An appeal against an administrative decision must be filed within sixty days of notification of that decision.
Article 115. The appellant may withdraw the appeal at any time before the hearing begins, by written notice to the registry.
Article 116. Where the appeal is withdrawn, the appellant bears the court fees in full.
Article 201. Procedural deadlines are suspended from the first to the thirty-first of August each year.
Article 202. A notice of appeal shall be in writing and signed by counsel admitted to practise before the court.
Article 203. Filings submitted through the certified electronic portal are accepted as of the date of transmission.
Article 310. The court shall issue its decision within ninety days of the close of the hearing.
Article 311. Where the appellant fails to appear at the hearing, the appeal is declared inadmissible.
Article 312. Deadlines run from the day following notification, and a deadline falling on a public holiday moves to the next working day.
Article 401. Legal costs are ordinarily recoverable by the successful party, unless the court orders otherwise.
Article 402. Either party may request that the hearing be expedited on grounds of demonstrated urgency.
Article 403. The registry shall serve the decision on all parties within ten days of its deposit.
Article 501. Evidence obtained unlawfully may not be relied upon in the proceedings.
Article 502. A witness summoned by the court who fails to attend may be fined.
Article 503. Expert reports shall be deposited at least fifteen days before the hearing.
Article 601. An application for interim relief may be made at any stage of the proceedings.
Article 602. Interim relief is granted only where irreparable harm would otherwise result.
Article 701. Court fees are set annually by ministerial decree and published in the official gazette.
Article 702. A party in financial hardship may apply for exemption from court fees.
Article 703. Fees paid in error are refunded on written application to the registry within one year.
